title: Guyana's Diaspora Bond: Promised in May, Still No Terms | Across the Water, Ep. 17
lede: On May 26, 2026, Guyana's 60th independence anniversary, President Irfaan Ali promised a diaspora bond within one week to fund public infrastructure. Nearly six months later, no bond has been issued and its size, rate, currency and eligibility are still undisclosed. On Nov 13 he said plans are advancing and assigned finance minister Ashni Singh to set the terms. This episode explains who the bond is aimed at, what diaspora bonds have raised elsewhere, and what to watch.
keyPoints: 36.4% of Guyana's native-born population lived abroad in 2020, the largest share of any country with 750,000+ people (UN data via Forbes/Stabroek News).
Ali promised the bond 'within one week' on May 26, 2026; on Nov 13 he put Senior Minister Ashni Singh in charge of its terms and framework (DPI; Guyana Chronicle).
The IMF projects 22.3% real growth for Guyana in 2026, with the fiscal deficit widening to 6.4% of GDP (IMF, Oct 8, 2026).
Workers' remittances to Guyana were US$444.4 million in 2025 (Bank of Guyana annual report, via La Caribeña News).
Israel Bonds have sold more than US$50 billion since 1951; India raised US$4.2 billion in 1998 and more than US$5.5 billion in 2000 (Israel Bonds; Migration Policy Institute).
